name: Benaiah
overview: Benaiah was a male Levite known as the son of Jeiel, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 20:14. His identification within the tribe of Levi situates him among those dedicated to religious duties in Israel. Beyond his parentage and tribal affiliation, the biblical text offers limited additional information about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Benaiah means 'YHWH has built,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew meaning. This proper name, recorded in 2 Chronicles 20:14, is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries the significance of divine establishment or construction.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Benaiah as the son of Jeiel, with an inferred relationship to Zechariah as his father. These familial ties are documented in 2 Chronicles 20:14. No further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Benaiah's mention as the son of Jeiel connects him to the Levitical lineage, which is significant for understanding the organization and personnel involved in temple service and religious activities. Although the biblical narrative does not elaborate extensively on his individual actions, his inclusion in the genealogical record underscores the importance of preserving the heritage of those serving in God's appointed roles. His name's meaning also subtly points to the faithfulness of God in establishing His people and their leaders.
